sources.entry: HardwareVisualizer - A cross-platform hardware monitor with real-time metrics, historical insights, and a customizable dashboard.

summary.one_liner: HardwareVisualizer is a desktop app for Windows, Linux, and macOS that shows live hardware metrics and keeps a local history of CPU, memory, GPU, and temperature data for later review.
keywords: check how hot my cpu runs
see if cooling is getting worse
summary.what_it_does: The app shows live CPU, memory, and GPU gauges and usage graphs, per-core usage, running processes, motherboard sensors and fans, and power draw, with Panels, Compact, and Monitor views. A System Specifications section lists CPU, GPU, memory, storage, platform, motherboard/BIOS, and network details and can produce a copyable hardware report, including SMART health for each drive. Insights keeps average, maximum, and minimum history for CPU, memory, CPU temperature, and per-GPU metrics for up to one year, plus process history for up to 30 days. Cooling Insight compares CPU temperature against its own baseline under similar load and plots it alongside load, package power, fan speed, and ambient temperature. A tray or menu bar widget shows CPU and GPU usage and GPU temperature. The README says hardware data stays on the local computer and that there is no telemetry; the app contacts the internet only to check GitHub Releases and, if chosen, to download PawnIO.
use_cases: monitor live cpu and gpu usage
check whether cpu temperature is rising over time
look up system specs and copy a hardware report
check smart health and temperature of drives
watch fan speed and power draw
keep a small hardware widget in the system tray
how_to_run: Windows: download the .msi (recommended) or .exe installer from GitHub Releases or hardviz.com, or run: winget install shm11C3.HardwareVisualizer
macOS: open the .dmg for Apple Silicon or Intel and drag HardwareVisualizer to Applications
Launch on Linux from the terminal with: hardware-visualizer
notable: Local-only hardware history retained for 365 days by default, with Insights charts for up to one year
Cooling Insight compares CPU temperature to its own baseline under similar load
Optional PawnIO integration enables CPU temperature, CPU package power, and motherboard fan/temperature sensors on Windows
Apple Silicon power draw for CPU, GPU, ANE, and package
Supports English, Japanese, and Russian UI languages
caveats: Many sensor features are Windows-only or limited: CPU temperature, power, and motherboard sensors are not available on Linux yet, and macOS has no GPU temperature or CPU temperature readings listed in the platform table.
Motherboard sensor support is limited to specific Nuvoton and ITE chips, several of which are marked experimental; Ambient temperature via SwitchBot is Windows-only.
Some readings need extra setup: PawnIO and administrator rights on Windows, smartctl and sudo or polkit on Linux.
